It took eighteen months to gently suggest to Shirley Rook that it would be the best policy for her to join us and eventually she made her decision and is now our number 1.

The team was greatly strengthened by the inclusion of a new Belgravian, Shirley Rook, a budding policewoman. Unfortunately on the first lap our other policewoman, Diane Cook, who had incidentally been on night duty all week, came under the judges ban - giving our team hopes a bit of a blow.

Shirley Rook beat Anna Matthews home by 1 second in the Southern Counties 5000 metre race on January 28th at Maidstone. They crossed the line in 5th and 6th places, 28:24 and 28:25, with Linda Nicholls not far away in 11th place, 30:49.

The Senior race saw Shirley Rook winning easily, her first Club Championship, from Anna Matthews. Congratulations to Joann Warnett on being picked to represent Greater London in the All England Schools Cross-Country Championships at Lincoln.

The first match meant a coach trip to Portsmouth where we had few winners but some fine performances from Shirley Rook (800m/1500m senior), Anne Slattery (senior javelin), Marjorie Woodward (3000m) and the 4 x 400m team made up of 3 field events girls Karen Smith, Wendy Dunsford, Anne Slattery and V…

Diane Cook was the highest placed of our ladies on April 8th at Ewell gaining 2nd over 3Km in the Senior Surrey Ladies Championship with 19:21. In the Intermediate 3Km Jane Pritchard was 5th in 18:20 while Shirley Rook was timed at 16:30 for 3rd in the open 3Km.
Most would have undoubtedly have settled on the former but Shirley Rook (20),to her credit, did the latter. As a result she helped Belgrave collect their first National Team Medals.
Well done Linda Nicholls for winning the Southern "Inter" title, and Shirley Rook and Anna Matthews for 2nd and 3rd in the Southern Senior race in the snow.
Derek Ellis was the Police Cadet Champion, Shirley Rook the National Police Champion (for running but she walks mostly) and John Dunsford placed 3rd in the European Veterans Championships.
